"Aesthetic Perfection Norm" introduces a social calibration point, and "Skill Salience Effect" demonstrates that effortful processes become focal points of attention. Together, they map onto predictive coding frameworks where familiar patterns generate minimal prediction error, whereas rare or difficult events cause large residuals. In GSI, these translate into anomaly detection and value identification; in GSE, they correspond to adaptive thresholding and situational awareness. The primitives fail when environments lack sufficient variation or when observers exhibit learned helplessness.
